subfigures.description: Left source subfigure, labelled Cyrillic a: one rounded eye outline with a small anterior bulge on the left and posterior retinal boundary on the right. Three approximately horizontal parallel incident rays (upper, axial, lower) travel left to right. The upper and lower rays refract inward at the front, meet on the axis inside the eye before the posterior boundary, cross, and reach that boundary separated again. The axial ray passes through the same meeting. The meeting and boundary points are unlabelled; there is no source focus-dot label.
points: unlabelled upper and lower anterior ray intersections
rays: upper parallel incident and crossed refracted ray
lower parallel incident and crossed refracted ray
subfigures.angles: No angle label or angle arc; parallel incident directions and post-refraction inward convergence followed by crossing are instructional relationships.
subfigures.givens: No dimensions, coordinates or numerical angles.

subfigures.description: Right source subfigure, labelled Cyrillic b: the same kind of rounded eye faces left. A vertical diverging spectacle-lens symbol stands before the eye, with top arrow pointing inward/down and bottom arrow pointing inward/up. Three parallel incident rays travel left to right. Upper/lower rays spread farther from the axis between spectacles and eye, then the eye refracts them inward to the posterior axial retinal point. Two dashed backward extensions of those spread rays meet at the open axial point A left of the spectacle lens. The axial ray runs through A, lens and posterior meeting.
points: A, an open point on the axis before the spectacle lens
unlabelled farther-separated upper/lower anterior eye intersections
rays: upper parallel incident, divergent after spectacle, convergent after eye
lower parallel incident, divergent after spectacle, convergent after eye
two dashed non-propagating backward extensions to A
subfigures.angles: No angle label or arc; upper/lower post-spectacle slopes point away from the axis and their backward extensions meet A.
subfigures.givens: Only A and the subfigure label; no distances or powers.

subfigures.description: Top subfigure, labelled Cyrillic a: a rounded eye with a left anterior bulge receives three parallel left-to-right incident rays, upper/axial/lower. The upper/lower rays slope inward after entering the eye, but remain separated at the posterior boundary; their source-drawn solid continuations meet on the axis just beyond that boundary. A short rightward continuation remains visible. This is a would-converge construction, not actual light propagation through a living retina.
points: unlabelled hypothetical axial focus behind retina
rays: upper/lower inward refracted rays still separated at retina
solid hypothetical continuations beyond retina and axial continuation
subfigures.angles: No angle label or arc; weaker inward convergence than needed to reach the retinal axis.
subfigures.givens: No distances, point letters or numerical angles.

subfigures.description: Middle subfigure, labelled Cyrillic b: a vertical converging spectacle-lens symbol, top arrow outward/up and bottom outward/down, precedes a rounded eye. Three parallel incident rays travel left to right. Upper/lower rays bend toward the axis at the spectacle lens, become closer together before entering the eye, and after the eye meet at the posterior axial retinal point. The axial ray remains straight.
points: unlabelled closer-separated upper/lower anterior eye intersections
rays: upper parallel incident, inward after spectacle, inward after eye
lower parallel incident, inward after spectacle, inward after eye
subfigures.angles: No angle label or arc; preconvergence before the eye is distinct from a diverging lens.
subfigures.givens: No distances, powers or named points.

subfigures.description: Bottom subfigure, labelled Cyrillic v: S is an axial object point before a converging spectacle-lens symbol with outward/up and outward/down tips. S1 is an open axial point farther left than S. Three source rays leave S toward the right: an upper divergent ray, axial ray and lower divergent ray. The upper/lower rays bend at the spectacle lens and continue toward the eye less divergently, then are refracted by the eye to the posterior retinal axis. Two dashed backward extensions of the less-divergent post-spectacle rays meet S1. The source's dimension d below runs from S1's vertical drop to a vertical drop at the eye front; it is not the distance from S to the lens. The source labels S and subscripted S1 and d; it does not print 25 cm inside the figure.
points: S1, open virtual-image point left of S
S, real axial object point left of spectacle lens
d endpoints vertically below S1 and the eye front
rays: three divergent or axial real incident rays from S
two dashed backward extensions from post-spectacle rays to S1
upper/lower eye-refracted rays and axial ray to retina
subfigures.angles: No angle labels or arcs; outgoing divergence is smaller than incoming divergence, while both stay divergent until the eye.
subfigures.givens: S, S1 and d only. Candidate text supplies conventional 25 cm and d > 25 cm under the stated near-viewing construction; 25 cm is not a universal near point.

modernAdditions: English a/b/c panel headings replacing Cyrillic labels; fig-186 panels stacked instead of side by side for 640 px readability.
Explicit thin-lens/paraxial, not-to-scale and accommodation-state annotations; these are model qualifiers from the candidate, not source pixel wording.
Retina labels and emphasis, tiny focus markers, and explicit hypothetical continuation annotation; no detailed anatomical or medical inference.
English S1 displayed as S1 rather than Cyrillic typography; S/S1/d/A relationships unchanged.
Near-panel conventional-reference and d > 25 cm notes may be added separately, never asserted as universal near-point or spectacle-prescription data.
Each panel independently regularizes schematic distances; no physical focal lengths, prescriptions or cross-panel quantitative scale are claimed.
